I'm a Brit, lived in the US for Ten Years working for  a UK Company, my American co-workers would not believe that in my home county of Cumbria we have houses with downspouts that are older than America is as a country. 
My American co-workers kept asking why I rarely ate out, and 'brown bagged' my lunch every day, when I told them that I reacted badly to what they classed as 'common safe foods' such as bread from supermarkets, and I scratch cooked everything even bread. 
If I had them round for dinner it was deff a culture shock for them to fresh veggies hanging in the kitchen , in cloth bags or nets  - a simple string of onions had them baffled as to why the were not rotting. 
I was lucky and found a small farm that grew and raised just about everything they ate, so I was able buy from them, veggies. beef, mutton (one of my favourite meats) milk, dairy, poultry, eggs (Chicken & Duck, that is another thing that confused those I had over for dinner, I had eggs out on the counter top not in the fridge, until i explained that the only reason that eggs were refrigerated in the US was the FDA mandating that eggs be washed, if poultry were given the chance to lay in a clean environment they didn't need to be washed) I paid the farmer more than I would have paid in a supermarket, but the quality was way better and they were good people and I was happy to pay the extra for the quality.

Ingredients
3 large egg whites
1/4 cup unflavored protein powder or egg white powder
1 tsp Italian Seasoning
¼ tsp salt
Toppings: Pizza Sauce, Pepperoni slices, Shredded Mozzarella
Instructions
Preheat the oven. Preheat your oven to 400°F (205°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and lightly grease it with nonstick spray.
Whip the egg whites. Add the egg whites to a large mixing bowl. Using an electric mixer or stand mixer, beat until very stiff peaks form. The mixture should look glossy and hold its shape when you lift the beaters.
Fold in the dry ingredients. Add the protein powder, salt, and Italian seasoning, if using. Gently fold everything together with a spatula until fully incorporated. Try not to overmix, so the egg whites stay fluffy.
Shape the crust. Spoon the mixture onto the prepared baking sheet and spread it into a 9-inch round crust. Keep the layer even so it bakes properly.
Bake the crust. Bake for 10–12 minutes, or until the crust is set, lightly golden around the edges, and firm enough to hold toppings.
Add toppings. Remove from the oven and add pizza sauce, mozzarella, pepperoni, or your favorite toppings.
Broil until melted. Broil for 3–4 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly. Watch closely so it doesn’t burn.  (from LowCarbSpark website)
